title: Autonomy Calendar And Coding Master Roadmap
goal: Bundle the remaining calendar/reminder automation work with autonomous coding production-readiness into a single backend-first execution plan.

source_roadmaps.title: Calendar MCP And Reminder Backbone Roadmap
source_roadmaps.why: Reliable reminders, todo digests and calendar context are daily operator infrastructure and directly fix the Telegram 09:00 reminder weakness.

source_roadmaps.title: Autonomous Coding Production Readiness Roadmap
source_roadmaps.why: Autonomous coding backend exists, but needs production-grade runner state, workstation-first scope resolution and remote monitoring/control.

source_roadmaps.title: Autonomous Coding Agent And Sandbox Execution Roadmap
source_roadmaps.why: Provides the completed sandbox, evidence and coding-agent foundation used by ACPR.

source_roadmaps.title: MCP Workbench Evidence Plan
source_roadmaps.why: Useful verification plane once available, but not a blocker for repo-only backend slices.

execution_order.reason: Confirm calendar/reminder current state before changing scheduler behavior.
Shared service first prevents Telegram, UI, native tools and MCP from diverging.
Directly fixes the five-tasks-for-one-weekday-reminder class of bugs.
Read-only MCP gives safe observability before writes.
Autonomous coding needs durable state before remote control matters.
Workstation-created roadmaps need bounded repo/path/check resolution.
Runner state must execute and consume sandbox checks through existing evidence contracts.
Remote pause/resume/status should consume the durable runner state, not drive the whole design.
Calendar MCP writes become safe after read-only resources and normalizer are proven.
Telegram reminder commands should use the capability layer once it exists.
Publish/deploy is last among repo-only coding work because it carries the largest blast radius.
After capability changes, refresh Odysseus self-knowledge and tool memory.
Run Telegram reminder, CalDAV writeback and workstation-to-Telegram coding smokes only after repo tests pass and operator Go is explicit.

safe_parallel_tracks.condition: different files except routes/coding_agent_routes.py; coordinate tests before commit
calendar MCP server and coding project scope are disjoint

tracks: task scheduler edits by any other roadmap
avoid_parallel_tracks.reason: scheduler/timezone behavior is fragile and should be edited serially

tracks: Telegram plugin edits from inbox or DSGVO tracks
avoid_parallel_tracks.reason: Telegram plugin is a hotspot and should be changed in narrow slices

live_go_required_for: Podman live job if not already bounded

definition_of_done: Calendar/reminder automation can create/update recurring Telegram reminders as one normalized task.
Calendar MCP exposes read resources and gated write tools.
CalDAV/Nextcloud readiness and pending writebacks are visible.
Autonomous coding tasks are workstation-first, durable, scoped and resumable.
Telegram can monitor/control coding tasks remotely without being the primary workspace.
Sandbox, quality, publish and deploy gates are explicit and auditable.
Maintenance self-knowledge refresh tells Odysseus about new calendar/coding capabilities.

recommended_next_slice.reason: CAL-MCP-0 through CAL-MCP-6 and ACPR-0 are complete; CAL-MCP-7 remains live-gated and ACPR-7 depends on the missing durable runner-state, so ACPR-2 is the next safe backend slice.
